sample.packing_or_protection: Custom in-place self-decoding packer (toolchain unidentified); obfuscated entry gate, import-table self-modification, GlobalFlags anti-debug checks, custom XOR+add+byteswap decode loop

executive_summary.one_sentence_summary: This file is a malicious, custom-packed loader that decrypts shellcode in memory to load a second program, but that second program never executed in this analysis, so its final behavior remains unknown.
executive_summary.plain_language_assessment: The file is a packer that hides its real work. When run, it passes an obfuscated entry check, decrypts a 1,728-byte block of hand-written shellcode, and hands control to that shellcode, which is a small loader built to map and run a second, larger program in memory. The second program never actually executed during this analysis, so what it would have done (such as contacting a command-and-control server or installing itself for persistence) is not established from this run. VirusTotal detects the file as malicious with 64 engines, but the public labels (rogue/fraudtool, 'spreader') and external indicators are from other sandboxes, not from this analysis. Treat the file as a loader whose real payload is yet to be confirmed.
executive_summary.remaining_decision_point: The actual capabilities of the final loaded payload (C2 endpoints, persistence mechanism, family identity) are not locally established; the role of decoded_stage2_raw.bin (a re-encode of the original sample's own data vs an independent embedded payload) remains open until a reproducible decode produces a loadable PE.

confirmed_findings.title: Malicious custom-packed loader
confirmed_findings.summary: The sample is a PE32 GUI binary (entry 0x401510) that is a malicious custom-packed loader, detected as malicious by 64 VirusTotal engines.

confirmed_findings.title: Obfuscated entry gate and anti-debug checks confirmed at runtime
confirmed_findings.summary: The packer uses an obfuscated entry gate (ROR-based, with a conditional crash path) that passed live into a chain of about 49 wrapper functions, and GlobalFlags/BeingDebugged anti-debug checks that detect a debugger but do not block execution.

confirmed_findings.title: Stage-1 shellcode recovered and validated
confirmed_findings.summary: A custom decode loop (key 0x22CC456A, XOR+add+byteswap) produces a validated 1,728-byte first-stage shellcode (decoded_payload.bin, sha256 9f8e4794...), independently hash-verified.

confirmed_findings.title: Stage-1 shellcode is a hand-written PE loader
confirmed_findings.summary: The shellcode finds kernel32.dll in memory, resolves Windows functions through a custom rolling hash, allocates executable memory, and is built to manually load a second program in memory. It contains no anti-VM, anti-debug, or timing checks.

findings_with_caveats.title: Recovered second-stage blob is real but not a valid loadable program
findings_with_caveats.summary: A 335,872-byte blob (decoded_stage2_raw.bin, sha256 0ec0a946...) exists and contains a parseable program header, but it is not a valid loadable PE and the documented attempt log records failures, so its origin could not be reproduced and no capabilities can be attributed from it.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: Do not treat decoded_stage2_raw.bin as a confirmed, recovered second-stage payload; its contents are unverified.

findings_with_caveats.title: Second stage is likely derived from the original file itself (self-reloading loader)
findings_with_caveats.summary: The stage-1 shellcode resolves file-mapping functions and the recovered second-stage header matches the original file's memory layout, suggesting the second stage is the original program mapped from disk rather than a separate embedded payload. This is a hypothesis, not a validated conclusion.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: This remains a hypothesis pending a reproducible decode of the original file region into a loadable program.

findings_with_caveats.title: Family attribution is not confirmed locally
findings_with_caveats.summary: Public labels (trojan.rogue/fraudtool, fakeav) and the 'spreader' tag come from VirusTotal; none establish a family identity and all require local confirmation in the never-loaded second stage.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: Treat the family labels and 'spreader' tag as follow-up context only, not confirmed identity.

findings_with_caveats.title: Stage-1 function hashes only partially identified
findings_with_caveats.summary: The shellcode resolves Windows functions by rolling hash; the hash algorithm and 16-entry table are confirmed, but the individual hash-to-name mapping was not computed, so the exact function list is partially inferred.
findings_with_caveats.caveat: Treat the resolved-function list as inferred, not definitive.

not_supported_claims.claim: The shellcode contains a distinct 0x6AC-byte second-stage PE embedded at offset 0x15.
not_supported_claims.reason: Deepdive rejected this claim as structurally impossible: it cannot fit in the 1,728-byte shellcode, and the bytes there are the shellcode's own code and data.
No C2, network, persistence, or credential behavior was observed locally; the public C2 endpoint is an external-only lead from VirusTotal sandboxes, not local evidence.

not_supported_claims.claim: Persistence behavior (RunOnce, AppData copy, IFEO, SafeBoot/Safer registry operations) was locally observed.
not_supported_claims.reason: Persistence was never locally observed; the RunOnce key and related registry activity are external-only VirusTotal sandbox observations and must be labeled as follow-up leads.

not_supported_claims.claim: A distinct second-stage payload executed locally.
not_supported_claims.reason: The second-stage PE never executed locally; no payload behavior beyond the stage-1 loader can be claimed.

not_supported_claims.claim: The sample's family is confirmed as rogue/fraudtool or fakeav (with a 'spreader' behavior).
not_supported_claims.reason: Family identity and the 'spreader' tag are public attribution hints only and were not confirmed locally.

classification.malware_type: packed loader / dropper (decodes a stage-1 shellcode that manually loads a second PE in memory)
classification.overall_assessment: The sample is a malicious custom-packed loader. Its first-stage shellcode (a hand-written PE loader) is validated, but the second-stage payload never executed locally, so its final capabilities (C2, persistence, family) remain unconfirmed; public labels are attribution hints only.

host.label: Original packed loader sample hash
host.note: Locally established sample identity; publicly detected as malicious by 64 engines.

host.label: Stage-1 shellcode hash (decoded_payload.bin)
host.note: Locally recovered and independently hash-verified 1,728-byte first-stage PE loader.

host.label: Stage-2 raw blob hash (decoded_stage2_raw.bin)
host.note: Locally recovered but NOT a validated payload: not a loadable PE and provenance unreproducible. Capabilities unknown.

recommended_actions.action: Reverse the exact decode semantics (config pe_offset/size, key 0x22CC456A) and decode candidate regions of the original file; compare to decoded_stage2_raw.bin to determine whether a loadable second-stage PE can be reconstructed.
recommended_actions.reason: This is the highest-value remaining decision point: it would establish the final payload's role and capabilities.

recommended_actions.action: Reconstruct a valid loadable PE header (correct DOS header and file-consistent section table) so the recovered stage-2 data can be statically analyzed for C2 config, persistence, and family.
recommended_actions.reason: The actual malware logic is expected to live in this stage; it currently cannot be loaded or analyzed.

recommended_actions.action: Reimplement the rolling hash and map all 16 entries to kernel32 function names to complete the loader's capability list.
recommended_actions.reason: Completes the stage-1 loader capability enumeration with little follow-up cost.

recommended_actions.action: Re-run the sample letting its own exception handler commit the decode destination (no debugger exception-skipping), then dump the mapped second stage at load completion.
recommended_actions.reason: A clean run should materialize the second stage in memory and allow local observation of the payload's real behavior.

recommended_actions.action: During a clean guest run, monitor for the public C2 requests (/api/urls/, /api/stats/install/), RunOnce writes, mutex open, and IFEO key before treating any of them as confirmed indicators.
recommended_actions.reason: These are follow-up leads only and become confirmed IOCs only if locally reproduced.

recommended_actions.action: Compare the wrapper-chain packer style and shared decode key against known packers and public samples once a stage-2 hash is available.
recommended_actions.reason: A concrete packer or family identification would materially improve detection guidance.

limitations: The second-stage PE never executed locally; all final-payload behavior (C2, persistence, family) is unknown, and absence during one run is not proof of nonexistence.
decoded_stage2_raw.bin's production is not reproducible from documented inputs and it is not a valid loadable PE, so no capabilities can be asserted from it.
The stage-1 shellcode was decoded analytically, not executed in-process, and its 16 API hashes are not fully mapped to function names.
The packer's anti-debug was observed only under one debugger; other environments were not stress-tested.
The external IOCs (C2 endpoint, RunOnce persistence) come from VirusTotal public sandboxes and are follow-up leads, not local observations.
The exact config-block semantics (pe_offset=0xB20400, size=0x40000) exceed the original file size on their face and are not yet explained.
